scope: Local semantic review of BROC as a persistent practice layer integrated into the existing Star and generation path.
findings: BROC prepares a medium-aware scene and bounded brief from the existing Star definition, versioned practice canon, and recent history; it saves the scene with the existing immutable attempt prompt. A legacy in-flight attempt without a scene stops safely instead of resuming outside BROC.

The existing image request service and publication path remain in use. Successful output is recorded as an unreviewed candidate; this integration does not inspect generated pixels or automatically promote work into canon.

Practice records are private and append-only, linked to existing Star actors and generation attempts. The local migration is additive, has a paired data-preserving rollback, and is not applied to the linked database.
No BROC application, route, public response field, Star registry, generation service, or deployment target was added. ADR 0161 remains proposed with local delivery evidence.

The compiled boundary scan inspected 526 browser/rendered assets without private markers or runtime trace paths. docs:impact reports only docs/knowledge/reviews.json and post-mortem/review.json as unmapped; these are self-referential review attestations, not product source files.

limits: The migration remains unapplied and the Star source integration is local only.
Pixel-level critique, explicit human direction controls, and automatic canon changes are not implemented by this integration.
The full generic database suite retains its separate existing asset-upload test failure; no unrelated repair was made.
